guidance.procedure: Read the complete definition as an operative chain: its lead-in, covered subject matter, communication forms, marking or designation conditions, and qualifications. For breadth, test whether coverage is confined to technical material or also reaches commercial, financial, business, visual, oral, or other information. For explicit identification, distinguish a universal marking requirement from reasonable-confidentiality language or coverage regardless of labeling. For oral inclusion, preserve any later written-confirmation condition. Cite every annotated fragment that jointly states the rule, including responsive continuations, but exclude headings, list introductions, and neighboring examples that add no proposition. Decide the relation only after checking the whole definition; lack of one formulation does not establish its opposite.

Separate four lifecycle issues before classifying: the trigger for return or destruction, whether the duty covers all or only some information, whether return and destruction are alternatives, and whether any copy may remain. A demand- or request-triggered duty is not automatically a termination-triggered duty. Read backup, archival, dispute, and legal-retention exceptions together with the main disposition rule; an exception can support permissible possession even while the main clause requires return or destruction. Evaluate survival from language continuing obligations beyond termination, not merely from a fixed agreement or confidentiality period. Cite independently responsive disposition, exception, and survival provisions, while excluding adjacent term language that does not answer the proposition.

Map the exact actor, recipient class, action, and condition. For sharing, distinguish employees from the broader classes of agents, contractors, advisers, affiliates, or unrestricted third parties. A need-to-know representative clause is different from a blanket disclosure right; a prohibition subject only to discretionary written consent may oppose a broad permission proposition rather than establish an affirmative contractual allowance. For copying, distinguish an absolute prohibition from a prohibition containing a purpose- or necessity-limited exception. Include each annotated operative access or copying clause and any separately responsive recipient restriction. Do not cite headings, generic confidentiality duties, or later duties merely because they are adjacent.

Inspect the exceptions architecture rather than isolated keywords. For independent development, require development without use of or access to protected information. For third-party acquisition, require an external source entitled to disclose and, where stated, absence of a confidentiality restriction; public-domain or prior-possession language is a different exception. For compelled disclosure, distinguish permission to comply from a duty to notify, and preserve prerequisites such as legal compulsion, permitted notice, protective-order opportunity, or limitation to the required portion. When annotations make both the exception lead-in and its subparagraph responsive, cite the complete chain. Do not substitute a neighboring exception or generic disclosure restriction.

Resolve each proposition into actor, modality, action, object, scope, and exception. Treat an express prohibition as responsive evidence for a prohibitory hypothesis. For reverse engineering, require language directed to reverse engineering or decompilation of protected information. For solicitation, require recruiting, soliciting, inducing, hiring, or comparable conduct aimed at the specified people, and preserve stated exceptions. For no-license propositions, require no-grant, no-license, or no-right language; ownership alone is not interchangeable. For confidentiality of the agreement, look for the agreement's existence, terms, or negotiations within protected information or an operative nondisclosure duty. For limited use, include clauses restricting use to the stated purpose and any independently annotated purpose provision, but not generic secrecy language.

Inspect the complete operative definition, not isolated nouns. For technical-only coverage, determine whether the protected class is exclusively technical; express inclusion of commercial, financial, business, oral, visual, or other material opposes that limitation. For explicit identification, require a universal marking or designation condition; broad confidentiality language alone is neutral, while coverage expressly independent of labeling opposes such a requirement. For oral information, include any designation and later written-confirmation conditions. Cite every fragment that completes the definition or condition, but exclude headings and illustrative material that adds no rule.

operations.rationale: The prior publication was followed by definition-related label losses and recurring incomplete or extraneous citations, including treating headings, examples, and neighboring definition fragments as operative evidence. This update makes the three propositions independent, adds both marking-required and labeling-independent contrasts, and narrows membership to fragments that actually complete the applicable rule.

guidance.procedure: Analyze disposition, retention, and survival separately. For return or destruction, identify the exact trigger: termination language can support the termination proposition, whereas a demand or request alone does not. Preserve whether the duty covers all information or only specified forms and whether return and destruction are alternatives. For post-disposition possession, an express backup, archive, legal-retention, or dispute exception supports retention; a requirement to return or destroy all information and copies without an exception supports the opposed boundary. For survival, require obligations expressly continuing beyond termination, not merely a fixed agreement term. Cite operative rules and responsive exceptions, not adjacent headings or enforcement clauses.

operations.rationale: Both observed batches repeatedly confused request-triggered return with termination-triggered return and reversed the effect of all-copy disposition clauses and retention exceptions. The earlier memory also produced lifecycle label harms. The replacement states the polarity boundary directly and uses compact opposed retention examples plus distinct termination and survival examples.

guidance.procedure: Decide each proposition independently by matching actor, action, recipient class, quantifier, and condition. Employee disclosure answers the employee proposition; consultants, agents, advisers, contractors, affiliates, or other non-employees may answer the third-party proposition only when the clause actually authorizes disclosure to that class. Preserve the observed distinction between an affirmative need-to-know authorization and a prohibition relieved only by discretionary written consent; do not turn the latter into a general permission. For copying, a necessity- or purpose-limited exception to a no-copy rule supports some permissible copying, while an unqualified no-copy duty supports opposition. Cite the operative authorization or prohibition and any fragment needed to state its condition, excluding recipient-notice duties and generic secrecy language.

operations.rationale: Sharing and copying remained a major source of polarity errors, cross-hypothesis transfer, missed members, and citations to adjacent duties. The previous false-citation example added substantial material without preventing those harms, so it is removed while the procedure and opposed member examples retain the substantive boundary.

guidance.procedure: Trace each exception as a grammatical chain from any operative exclusion lead-in to the responsive subparagraph. Independent development requires development without use of, reference to, or access to protected information. Third-party acquisition requires an external source entitled to disclose and, when stated, free of a confidentiality duty; public-domain and prior-possession exceptions are not substitutes. Compelled disclosure permission and a notice duty are separate: verify legal compulsion, whether notice is required or excused, protective-order opportunity, and any required-portion limit. Cite the lead-in when it supplies the exclusion or scope and every responsive continuation, but not a standalone heading or neighboring exception.

operations.rationale: Current observations continued to omit exception lead-ins or responsive qualifications and sometimes added neighboring exceptions. A compact, internally consistent set now demonstrates all three exception structures, while removal of the longer prior examples and false-citation contrast reduces distraction and materialized size.

guidance.procedure: Resolve actor, modality, action, object, scope, and exceptions before choosing a relation. Reverse engineering requires direct reverse-engineer, decompile, test, or equivalent language concerning protected material; confidentiality, copying, ownership, or ordinary use restrictions are not substitutes. Solicitation requires recruiting, soliciting, inducing departure, hiring, or comparable conduct directed at the specified people, including all fragments carrying the actor and exceptions. No-license requires express no-grant, no-license, or no-right language; ownership alone is insufficient. Agreement confidentiality requires protection of its existence, terms, or negotiations. Limited use requires an operative restriction to the stated purpose, together with any operative purpose definition that delimits it, not generic secrecy language or a heading.

operations.rationale: The memory-backed runs introduced unsupported reverse-engineering findings, missed multi-fragment solicitation evidence, and over-cited confidentiality, recipient, and heading text for limited-use questions. This update adds a confidentiality-of-agreement witness, retains direct-action examples, and expressly blocks substitution among ownership, copying, secrecy, use, and reverse engineering.
